llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (fetching and presenting Douyin hot lists) but contains several implementation and instruction choices that are disproportionate or suspicious—most notably raw-socket HTTPS calls with certificate/SNI checks disabled and mandatory automated output/persistence behaviors not justified by the description.

dimensions.detail: The skill's files (hotspot_fetcher.py and gen_douyin_hot_html.py) implement the advertised functionality (fetching Douyin hotlist data and generating an HTML report). However the network code is unusual: it connects to a hardcoded IP (8.154.41.7) for host onetotenvip.com using raw sockets, disables TLS verification (context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE / check_hostname = False) and does not send SNI. These low-level choices are not necessary to fetch a public JSON API and are disproportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires the agent to strictly follow assets/core-workflow.md and execute scripts that (a) must immediately generate HTML and PDF files, (b) must output the complete HTML source in the agent reply, and (c) must handle subscription recording and automatic hourly/daily pushes. Forcing automatic generation and full inline output of potentially large HTML/PDF content (and API-returned URLs/content) without explicit user confirmation is overbroad and risky. The subscription/push behavior is specified but no storage/config path or scheduling mechanism is declared.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec: this is an instruction-and-script-only skill. No external installers or downloads are invoked by the skill bundle itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request any environment variables or credentials. That is proportionate to a read-only data-fetching/reporting tool. Note: the subscription feature claims to 'record preferences' but the skill does not declare any config path or credential for persistent storage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-installed (always:false) and can be invoked normally. However SKILL.md demands recording subscription preferences and scheduling hourly pushes; that implies persistent background behavior but no mechanism (no config paths, no scheduler, no declared service account) is provided. This mismatch is a design/incoherence concern (the skill asks for persistence in behavior but doesn't declare how it will persist or run).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- The core functionality (fetching Douyin hot lists and producing an HTML report) matches the skill description, but the implementation uses an unusual and risky network approach: it connects to a hardcoded IP for onetotenvip.com, disables TLS certificate verification and omits SNI. This can be used to bypass normal TLS protections or to reach a hostile/opaque endpoint—treat that as a red flag.

- The skill's runtime instructions force immediate generation and inline output of complete HTML and PDF content and ask the agent to record subscription preferences for hourly/daily pushes. That behavior can cause large unsolicited outputs, include external URLs returned by the API in chat replies, and implies persistence without explaining where or how preferences are stored or how scheduling occurs.

- If you still want to use it: run the Python scripts in an isolated environment (air-gapped or sandbox), inspect/modify the network code to use a standard HTTP client (requests) with proper certificate validation, change hardcoded IPs to hostnames or verify the API owner, and modify the SKILL.md behavior so that HTML/PDF generation and subscriptions happen only after explicit user consent. Avoid installing or granting persistent background privileges until the subscription/persistence mechanism is clearly and securely implemented.

- If you cannot audit or modify the code, do not install from this unknown source and avoid giving it autonomous/always-on privileges.
